answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using hardware remote attestation. Agents execute inside secure enclaves, signing state proofs with a cryptographic quill rooted in silicon. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable hardware cost of physical processor chips instead of branching a synthetic vine of software clones. Peers admit identities through a saffron attestation gate. However, reliance on centralized chipmakers creates vendor lock-in and side-channel vulnerabilities.
